options.content:
**Connectors Detail: Databases**: one collapsed row per database connector (MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, Snowflake), built from that connector's per-cluster boards (overview, pipeline, runtime). Expand a row for its full detail. Each row shows everything in namespace `default`; the Scanner/Content component pickers at the top apply to their connector's row. For per-pod, query-type or datasource-id filtering, open the per-cluster board linked in each section header. Each section header links to the per-cluster board it came from. The file, storage and document connectors (CIFS, Box, SharePoint, S3, Xberg) are on Connectors Detail: Files & Documents.

_Generated by `tools/build-detail.py` from 12 per-cluster boards. Do not edit this board in Grafana or by hand: edit the source board and re-run the script._

### MySQL Connector — Overview
Generated from `dashboards/applications/V2/connectors/mysql/mysql-overview.json` · per-cluster board: [MySQL Connector — Overview](/d/apps-v2-mysql-overview)

panels.title: Connections (Open)
panels.description: Open MySQL connections summed across every active scanner pool. Pools are per-datasource and created/evicted at runtime, so this is a scrape-time aggregate, not a fixed ceiling.

panels.title: ScanStart In Flight
panels.description: ScanStart handler invocations currently doing database discovery and DatabaseFork fan-out. The per-table leaf work that runs after fan-out is counted separately (see Tables In Flight on the pipeline dashboard).

panels.title: Items Sent (5m)
panels.description: Items successfully submitted through ItemBatchSender.UpsertItem, per second.

panels.title: Scan p95 (5m)
panels.description: p95 of the ScanStart discovery + fan-out phase. Histogram ladder is 0.5s to ~1024s, so this measures how long it takes to enumerate databases and hand out work — not how long a whole scan takes end to end.

panels.title: Error Rate (5m)
panels.description: Query failures against the source database, per second: database_errors_total + table_errors_total. Skipped tables and connector bugs are counted apart — see the Silent-Failure Signals row.

panels.title: Table Panics (5m)
panels.description: Leaf-worker tasks that panicked. Always a connector bug, never a source-database fault — counted apart from table_errors_total so a panic on an unexpected column shape doesn't read as the customer's MySQL refusing a query. Any non-zero value is worth acting on.

panels.title: Inline Fallback (5m)
panels.description: Tables the worker pool refused, run inline on the NATS consumer goroutine instead of being dropped. The pool only refuses after Shutdown, so non-zero means a scan was still fanning out while the process was tearing down — accounting stays exact, but the rest of that database serialises onto one goroutine.

panels.title: No Visible Columns (5m)
panels.description: Tables skipped because INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS returned no rows — a missing column-level GRANT, or a table dropped mid-scan. The query succeeded, so this is not a query failure. Alert on a sustained rate, not on any non-zero value.

panels.title: Error Reports Dropped (5m)
panels.description: Structured errors that never reached the observer, across all reasons (buffer_full, after_close, publish_failed). Non-zero means the job record is showing a truncated view of the scan's failures. Break down by reason on the pipeline dashboard.

panels.title: Connections (Open)
panels.description: Open MySQL connections summed across active content-fetch pools. A climb that does not come back down alongside a non-zero Conn Discard failure is the pool-exhaustion signature described on that panel.

panels.title: Fetch In Flight
panels.description: Content fetch requests currently being processed.

panels.title: Fetch p95 (5m)
panels.description: p95 end-to-end fetch latency for successful requests only: handler entry (URN parse, datasource resolve, conn acquire) through stream completion and reply publish. Errors are filtered out so a fast failure doesn't flatter the number.

panels.title: Errors (5m)
panels.description: Content requests that errored in the last 5 minutes — counter increase on mysql_content_requests_total{outcome="error"}.

panels.title: Content Fetch Duration — p50 / p95 / p99
Producer Panics (5m)
panels.description: Streaming producers that panicked and were recovered. Always a connector bug: the requester is told INTERNAL/retryable and the message is redelivered, so nothing in the request's own outcome says this connector crashed.

panels.title: Byte Mismatch (5m)
panels.description: Uploads whose stored size disagreed with the sampled/streamed byte count. The handler NAKs without replying, so a single count is a transient that a redelivery repaired; a sustained rate means the same URN fails verification every attempt, and once MaxDeliver is spent the object proven wrong stays under that URN with no reply ever sent.

panels.title: Conn Discard Failures (5m)
panels.description: Abandoned result sets whose connection could NOT be discarded (outcome != "discarded"). The discard is the only defence against the driver's uncancellable drain of the rest of a multi-GB column — a drain that ignores the query deadline and SIGTERM while holding a pool connection and a worker slot. Non-zero means the byte budget stops bounding what crosses the wire, and the symptom surfaces as pool exhaustion rather than an error.

panels.title: Sample Re-draws (5m)
panels.description: Content fetches whose first random draw fell under MYSQL_CONTENT_SAMPLE_MIN_ROWS and were re-drawn at a higher percent, all outcomes summed. Each re-draw is an extra table scan, so a sustained rate means MYSQL_CONTENT_SAMPLE_PERCENT is set too low for the tables being classified — raise the percent, not the floor. Break down by outcome on the pipeline dashboard: "failed" is a different problem and points at the query timeout and the source database.

### MySQL Connector — Pipeline
Generated from `dashboards/applications/V2/connectors/mysql/mysql-pipeline.json` · per-cluster board: [MySQL Connector — Pipeline](/d/apps-v2-mysql-pipeline)

panels.title: Tables & Columns Discovered (rate)
panels.description: Tables successfully scanned and columns retrieved, per second. Tables that failed or were skipped are not in these counters — see the Errors & Silent Failures row.

panels.title: Items & Batches Sent (rate)
panels.description: items/s is the connector's own mysql_scanner_items_sent_total. The other two come from the shared ItemBatchSender in pipeline-lib-go and carry no connector prefix, so they are filtered by job — batches/s is how often the batch is flushed to JobEngine.

panels.title: Scan Duration — p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: ScanStart database discovery + fan-out phase, on a 0.5s–1024s ladder. This runs on the single pod that received the ScanStart message; the leaf work it hands out is not included.

panels.title: Scanner Errors (rate)
panels.description: Query failures against the source database. These are the only two counters that mean "MySQL refused something" — everything on the next two panels is deliberately kept out of them.

panels.title: Skips & Connector Bugs (count, 5m)
panels.description: Three failure modes counted apart from table_errors_total because none of them is the source database's fault. no visible columns — INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS returned nothing (missing column-level GRANT, or a table dropped mid-scan); alert on a sustained rate, not any non-zero value. inline fallback — the worker pool refused a table after Shutdown and the scanner ran it on the consumer goroutine, serialising the rest of that database. table panics — always a connector bug, any non-zero value is worth acting on.

panels.title: Error Reporter Drops by Reason (count, 5m)
panels.description: Structured errors that never reached the observer, so the job record is showing a truncated view of the scan's failures. buffer_full — the buffered channel saturated. after_close — PublishError called after Close. publish_failed — the observer refused or could not be reached; this is the remote failure mode, and without it an unreachable observer used to lose every ItemError while the drop counter stayed at zero. close timeouts counts one abandonment of an unknown number of reports rather than individual errors, which is why it is a separate series: reaching it means publishLoop was parked inside a single publish for the whole flush budget, so check the control plane's health, not the scan.

panels.title: Error Reporter — Abandoned Flushes (live)
panels.description: Abandoned error-reporter flushes whose background goroutine is still parked in a publish — a live count on this pod, not a rate. Its sibling on the panel to the left counts how many times an abandonment has happened since the pod started; this one is how many are outstanding right now, which is the number that says whether the pod is still healthy. The two differ because an ErrorReporter is built and closed per message (one per ScanStart, one per DatabaseFork): an abandoned flush leaves a goroutine plus its 100-slot buffer behind, and the error that Close's caller returns NAKs the message, so redelivery supplies another fork that does it again. It unwinds on its own — each goroutine exits as soon as its publish returns — so a value that climbs and stays up is a control plane that is not answering, not a leak the connector can close from the inside. On the pinned pipeline-lib-go that publish resolves the job's step through GetJobSettings on a context with no deadline, which is why there is nothing bounding it below the reporter's 5s flush budget. Sustained above zero is alert-worthy; check the control plane, not the scan.

panels.title: Query Duration Heatmap
panels.description: Scanner-path SQL latency distribution, on a 10ms–20s ladder.

panels.title: Query p95 by query_type
panels.description: query_type is list_tables (INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES per database) or query_columns (INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS per table). A list_tables p95 climbing alone points at a database with a very wide table count; query_columns climbing points at the tables themselves.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, query_type) (rate(mysql_scanner_query_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$mysql_pod", query_type=~"$mysql_query_type"}[5m])))

panels.title: Scanner Connections by Type
panels.description: Aggregated across every active scanner pool at scrape time. in-use pinned at open with idle at zero is the pool running at its ceiling.

panels.title: Scanner — In Flight
panels.description: scanstart is the discovery + fan-out phase on the pod that received ScanStart. tables (leaf pool) is the per-table work the fan-out handed to the worker pool — the two are counted separately on purpose, so a busy leaf pool does not look like a stuck ScanStart.

panels.title: Query Rate by query_type
panels.description: Observation count on the query-duration histogram — how many scanner-path queries are actually being issued, split by kind.

panels.title: Fetch Duration — p50 / p95 / p99 by outcome
panels.description: End-to-end request latency, split by outcome so a fast failure does not flatter the success distribution: handler entry (URN parse, datasource resolve, conn acquire) through stream completion and reply publish.

panels.title: Stream Duration — p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: The streaming pipeline only — from the producer goroutine pulling its first row out of MySQL until UploadFrom returns. Excludes handler setup. Query and upload run concurrently, so this reflects whichever leg is slower at any moment; the gap between this and Fetch Duration is setup cost.

panels.title: Stream Bytes — p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: Bytes per successful fetch, taken from UploadResponse.Size — the count the content transfer service actually stored, not Info.Size, which this connector leaves at 0 because a sample's length is unknown until the last row streams. Ladder runs 1KiB to 4GiB.

panels.title: Stream Throughput (bytes/s)
panels.description: Sum of stored bytes per second across successful fetches.

panels.title: Stream Rows — Rate (rows/s)
panels.description: Sampled rows written per second across successful fetches.

panels.title: Stream Rows — Avg per Fetch
panels.description: Average sampled rows per successful fetch (sum / count over the window). Compare against MYSQL_CONTENT_SAMPLE_MIN_ROWS and MAX_ROWS: sitting at the ceiling means the sampler is being capped, sitting at the floor means it is being rescued by re-draws.

panels.title: Sample Re-draws by Outcome (count, 5m)
panels.description: Fetches whose first draw fell under MYSQL_CONTENT_SAMPLE_MIN_ROWS and were re-drawn at a higher percent. recovered — a later draw reached the floor. short — every draw stayed under it, and since the final draw runs at 100% that means the column genuinely holds fewer non-NULL values than the floor, not a sampling miss. failed — a draw errored before finishing, so its row count says nothing about the column; kept separate so a broken query is not read as a small column. A fourth case carries no label and appears in none of these: a draw torn down because the upload died. During a content-service outage the three series therefore do not sum to the number of fetches that re-drew. Sustained recovered/short means raise MYSQL_CONTENT_SAMPLE_PERCENT, not the floor — each re-draw is an extra table scan. Sustained failed is a different problem: look at the query timeout and the source database.

panels.title: Sample Percent Used
panels.description: The percent the streamed draw actually ran at. It equals MYSQL_CONTENT_SAMPLE_PERCENT whenever the first draw was kept, so drift above the configured value is the signal that the row floor is doing the work instead of the percent.

panels.title: Conn Discard by Outcome (count, 5m)
panels.description: Abandoned result sets whose driver connection was thrown away rather than drained. discarded — the connection was closed so the driver skips its post-finish drain; the intended path. unsupported — the Querier exposed no raw connection, so nothing could be closed and the DSN's ReadTimeout is the only bound left on the drain. close_error — the raw-connection callback or the Close itself failed, so the drain very likely still happened. Anything other than discarded is worth alerting on: the byte budget stops bounding what crosses the wire, and the symptom is pool exhaustion rather than an error anyone would connect back to sampling.

panels.title: Content Bugs (count, 5m)
panels.description: producer panics — a streaming producer panicked and was recovered; the requester is told INTERNAL/retryable and the message is redelivered, so nothing in the request's own outcome says this connector crashed. byte mismatch — the stored size disagreed with what was sampled and streamed; the handler NAKs without replying, so one count is a transient a redelivery repaired, while a repeating one means the same URN fails verification every attempt and once MaxDeliver is spent the object proven wrong stays under that URN with no reply ever sent.

panels.title: Content Connections (Open) by Pod
panels.description: Per-pod so one replica leaking connections stands out from the aggregate.

panels.title: Connection Tests by Outcome
panels.description:
**Connection tests answered in the selected range**, by outcome: success, partial (some objects could not be read), credential_error, permission_denied, timeout, error, publish_failed.

A test interrupted by this pod shutting down is redelivered to another pod and counted there.

**Next:** 'Connection Test Outcomes (rate, 5m)' beside it for when they happened; the connector logs carry the classified error_code of each failure.

targets.expr: sum by (outcome) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(mysql_connectiontest_requests_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$mysql_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(mysql_connectiontest_requests_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$mysql_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(mysql_connectiontest_requests_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$mysql_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) > 0

panels.title: Connection Test Outcomes (rate, 5m)
panels.description: When connection tests were answered, by outcome. A test shorter than a scrape interval can read 0 here and still be counted in 'Connection Tests by Outcome'.

panels.title: Connection Test Duration by Depth (p95)
panels.description: End-to-end time to answer a connection test, from receiving the request to publishing the reply, by requested depth. Deeper tests list more objects and take longer.

panels.title: Connection Test Objects Skipped (rate, 5m)
panels.description: Objects a connection test could not read and reported on their own node while it carried on, by level. A test with any is answered with the partial outcome.

### MySQL Connector — Runtime
Generated from `dashboards/applications/V2/connectors/mysql/mysql-runtime.json` · per-cluster board: [MySQL Connector — Runtime](/d/apps-v2-mysql-runtime)

panels.title: Container CPU Usage
panels.description: cAdvisor series, so it is selected by pod name rather than by job — the Component variable does not filter this panel.

panels.title: Container Memory (working set)
panels.description: cAdvisor series, so it is selected by pod name rather than by job — the Component variable does not filter this panel. This is the number the OOM killer watches, not process RSS.

panels.title: Goroutines
panels.description: A count that climbs and never comes back down across scans is the leak signature — the leaf worker pool and the content streaming producers are the two places goroutines are spawned per unit of work.

panels.title: GC Pause (max / p75)
panels.description: go_gc_duration_seconds is a SUMMARY, not a histogram — there is no _bucket series, so histogram_quantile against it returns nothing. These are the pre-computed quantiles the Go collector exports; the available ones are 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 1, so there is no p99 to plot. The label is matched with =~ because client_golang formats these values as "0.0"/"1.0" here while older versions emit "0"/"1" — an exact quantile="1" silently returns nothing.

panels.title: GC Cycles (rate)
panels.description: Completed GC cycles per second, from the summary's observation count. A rate that climbs alongside flat heap in-use means allocation churn rather than growth.

panels.title: Open vs Max FDs
panels.description: Every pooled MySQL connection is a socket, so an open count converging on max is how connection-pool exhaustion presents at the process level.

panels.title: Probe Duration by Depth
panels.description: Time spent discovering objects (databases, schemas, tables, columns) after the connection is open, by requested depth. Credential fetch and the connect itself are excluded.

panels.title: Peak Tests In Flight
panels.description: Most connection tests this connector was answering at once in the selected range.

### PostgreSQL Connector — Overview
Generated from `dashboards/applications/V2/connectors/postgresql/postgresql-overview.json` · per-cluster board: [PostgreSQL Connector — Overview](/d/apps-v2-postgresql-overview)

**Totals add up every scan in the time range.** Two scans of a 139-table server read 278 tables. To count what the server holds, narrow the range to one scan.

**Bars and stats say _how many_. The line charts beside them say _when_.** A scan shorter than ~30 seconds can be invisible on a line chart and still be fully counted in the bars.

**One item = one column.** PostgreSQL sends no table documents, so Items Sent should equal Columns Found exactly.

**What this board cannot tell you:** anything per datasource, per database or per schema (the metrics carry none of those labels — the dead-letter messages and the logs do name them); how many connections PostgreSQL is holding (nothing measures it); and how long a scan took end to end (nothing times it: 'Scan Duration' is read off the first and last activity, ±15 s).

Hover the ⓘ on any panel for what it counts, what is normal, and where to look next.

panels.title: Duration ±15s
panels.description:
**How long the scan took, end to end**: from the moment its databases were listed to the last table read. With several scans in the range it spans all of them, idle gaps included.

**Normal:** seconds to minutes, precise to about ±15 s: it is read from samples taken every 10–30 s, not timed. **0 s means the whole scan fit between two samples** — it ran and was fast (a 144-table server scans in about a second); the counts beside it show what it did.

**Next:** 'Fan-out over time' in the Scanner row shows the same span as a shape.

targets.expr: max_over_time(timestamp(sum(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) * 1)) > 0)[$__range:15s]) - min_over_time(timestamp(sum(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_databases_discovered_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_databases_discovered_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_databases_discovered_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) * 1)) > 0)[$__range:15s])

panels.title: Databases
panels.description:
**Databases the scan found on the server** and handed out to be scanned, after the configured exclusions.

**Normal:** the number of databases the scan account can see, once per scan in the range.

**Next:** 'Database Failures' in Scan Health for the ones that could not be opened.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_databases_discovered_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_databases_discovered_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_databases_discovered_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Schemas
panels.description:
**Schemas found across those databases**, system schemas excluded.

**Normal:** the user schemas of every scanned database.

**Next:** 'Schemas by Scan Mode' in the funnel for how each one was read.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_schemas_discovered_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_schemas_discovered_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_schemas_discovered_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Tables
panels.description:
**Tables, views, materialized views and foreign tables whose columns were read.**

**Normal:** every relation of every scanned schema. A relation with no columns is skipped in bulk mode and counted in table mode.

**Next:** 'Tables by Outcome' in the funnel.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Columns
panels.description:
**Columns read across all scanned tables.** Each one becomes one item.

**Normal:** roughly tables × average width ('Columns per Table' on the Pipeline board).

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_columns_found_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_columns_found_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_columns_found_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Items Sent
panels.description:
**Items handed to the sender for indexing**, one per column. Counted when queued: a batch that then fails to reach the message queue is not subtracted.

**Normal:** exactly Columns Found.

**Next:** 'Items Lost' beside it.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_items_sent_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_items_sent_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_items_sent_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Items Lost
panels.description:
**Columns found but never handed on for indexing**: Columns Found minus Items Sent.

**Normal:** 0. Above 0 means those columns are missing from the index while the scan still finishes green.

**Next:** 'Columns Lost' in Scan Health, and the scanner logs ('buildDocuments', 'Failed to upsert item').

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_columns_found_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_columns_found_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_columns_found_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0)) - ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_items_sent_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_items_sent_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_items_sent_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Fetches
panels.description:
**Column samples requested from the content side**, any outcome. Content runs on its own pods, triggered separately from scans.

**Normal:** whatever the downstream classifier asked for; 0 when nothing requested samples.

**Next:** the Content row.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_fetch_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_fetch_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_content_fetch_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go-content"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Funnel — Database → Schema → Table → Column → Item
Schema Attempts
panels.description:
**Times a schema was read — attempts, not schemas.** A schema that fails temporarily is retried, up to 5 times, and every try counts here.

**Normal:** equal to Schemas Discovered. Above it means schemas are failing and being retried.

**Next:** 'NATS Redelivered' in the Scanner row and 'Work Lost (DLQ)' beside it.

panels.title: NATS Backlog
panels.description:
**Work waiting in the queue** (stream JE_POSTGRESQL): scan requests, databases and schemas not picked up yet. This is 'how far behind is it?', and it is readable even while the connector is asleep.

**Normal:** 0 between scans. Growing with no pods running means the connector is not waking up.

panels.title: NATS In Flight
panels.description:
**Work handed to a pod and not finished yet.** Each message is a whole database or schema.

**Normal:** a few while a scan runs, 0 otherwise. Stuck above 0 while nothing is being scanned means a pod is hung.

panels.title: NATS Redelivered
panels.description:
**Work being retried after a failure.** A database or schema is retried up to 5 times before going to the dead-letter queue.

**Normal:** 0. A connector failing and retrying in a loop shows up here and nowhere else.

**Next:** Scan Health for what is failing.

panels.title: Replicas
panels.description:
**Scanner pods running now**, as the autoscaler reports them.

**Normal:** 0 between scans, a few during one.

panels.title: Max Replicas
panels.description:
**The most scanner pods the autoscaler may start** (chart setting autoscaling.maxReplicas, 10 by default).

**Normal:** read it against Replicas: at the ceiling with a growing backlog means the scanner cannot go faster.

panels.title: Backlog Slope (2m)
panels.description:
**How fast the backlog is growing**, in messages per second. This is exactly what one of the autoscaler's rules looks at.

**Normal:** 0. Above 0.5 the autoscaler adds pods.

panels.title: NATS — Scanner Consumer Backlog
panels.description:
**The queue over time.** Pending = waiting, ack pending = being worked on, redelivered = being retried. Each message is a scan request, a database or a schema, so 3 pending can be three entire schemas.

**Normal:** spikes at the start of a scan that drain to 0.

panels.title: KEDA — Replicas: current vs desired vs max
panels.description:
**Pods running, pods wanted, and the ceiling.**

**Normal:** pods stay up ~5–10 minutes after the work ends (cooldown 300 s, scale-down window 300 s, at most half the pods removed per minute). 'It scaled minutes ago and is still the same' is configuration, not a bug.

panels.title: Pods Up
panels.description:
**Scanner pods answering right now.**

**Normal:** 0 when idle — the scanner scales to zero between scans. That is not an outage.

panels.title: Restarts (1h)
panels.description:
**Scanner container restarts in the last hour.**

**Normal:** 0. Usually the pod ran out of memory (limit 1 GiB) or failed its health check; the work it held is retried.

**Next:** the Runtime board.

panels.description:

**Normal:** well under a second.

**Next:** 'Duration ±15s' in Totals for the whole scan.

**Tables each pod was reading at once**, highest value in each minute. The red line is the per-pod ceiling (20).

### PostgreSQL Connector — Pipeline
Generated from `dashboards/applications/V2/connectors/postgresql/postgresql-pipeline.json` · per-cluster board: [PostgreSQL Connector — Pipeline](/d/apps-v2-postgresql-pipeline)

**This is the drill-down.** The Overview says *what happened*; this board says *how much it cost* and *how it was distributed*. Nothing here is repeated from the Overview.

**Totals add up every scan in the time range** — narrow the range to one scan to describe one server.

**Time here is database time** — how long the scanner waited on PostgreSQL. Nothing times the connector's own work per table, and queries run in parallel, so a scan takes less wall-clock time than the sum shown here.

**The query type selector** at the top narrows the query panels to one kind of query.

Hover the ⓘ on any panel for what it counts, what is normal, and where to look next.

panels.title: Database Time per Table
panels.description:
**Average time PostgreSQL spent answering the scanner, per table**, in milliseconds: every query of the scan (listings, columns, permissions) divided by tables scanned.

**Normal:** a few to tens of ms. Multiply by the number of tables for the database time of a bigger server; the wall-clock scan is shorter because up to 20 tables per pod run in parallel.

**Next:** 'Query Time by Type' on the Overview for which query dominates.

targets.expr: 1000 * sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_query_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_query_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_query_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) / (sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) > 0)

panels.title: Database Time per Column
panels.description:
**The same database time divided by columns instead of tables**, in milliseconds. Columns are read together (one query per table, or per schema in bulk), so this is not how long one column takes.

**Normal:** well under a millisecond in bulk mode. If it stays flat while time per table moves, the tables got wider, not slower.

targets.expr: 1000 * sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_query_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_query_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_query_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) / (sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(postgresql_connector_columns_found_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) - last_over_time(postgresql_connector_columns_found_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(postgresql_connector_columns_found_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$postgresql_pod", job=~".*postgresql-connector-be-go"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) > 0)

panels.title: Query Duration — distribution
panels.description:
**How long each SQL query took, over time**, filtered by the Query type selector. **How to read it:** time runs left to right, the measured value bottom to top. Each box is 'this many fell in this range, at this moment' — brighter = more; hover a box for the exact count (Value). Colours do not identify individual items.

### PostgreSQL Connector — Runtime
Generated from `dashboards/applications/V2/connectors/postgresql/postgresql-runtime.json` · per-cluster board: [PostgreSQL Connector — Runtime](/d/apps-v2-postgresql-runtime)

**Is the connector itself healthy?** CPU, memory, Go runtime and file handles for the scanner and content pods. Use the *component* selector at the top to look at one of them.

**Empty is normal:** both deployments scale to zero between jobs, so this board only has data while something runs.

Hover the ⓘ on any panel for what it shows, what is normal, and where to look next.

panels.title: Process CPU (rate)
panels.description:
**CPU the connector process uses**, in cores.

**Normal:** near 0 when idle, up to the limit during work (0.5 core for the scanner, 0.25 for content). Pinned at the limit means the pod is being throttled and everything slows down.

**Next:** 'Container CPU Usage' for what Kubernetes sees.

panels.title: Process Resident Memory
panels.description:
**Memory the process is really using** (what is in RAM).

**Normal:** well below the limit (1 GiB scanner, 512 MiB content). A line that only goes up across several scans points at memory that is never released — e.g. the scans a scanner pod keeps cached, with their connection pools, for 30 minutes after their last message (jobContextIdleTTL).

**Next:** 'Container Memory (working set)' for the number Kubernetes compares with the limit.

panels.title: Process Virtual Memory
panels.description:
**Memory the process has reserved**, used or not. Go reserves far more than it uses.

**Normal:** large and flat. Not a useful alarm on its own — use resident memory.

panels.title: Container CPU Usage
panels.description:
**CPU per pod as Kubernetes measures it.** These container panels select pods by name, because Kubernetes' own metrics do not carry the connector's labels.

**Normal:** same shape as Process CPU. At the limit (0.5 core scanner, 0.25 content) the pod is throttled.

panels.title: Container Memory (working set)
panels.description:
**Memory per pod as Kubernetes measures it** — the number it compares with the limit (1 GiB scanner, 512 MiB content).

**Normal:** well below the limit. Reaching it gets the pod killed (OOMKilled) and the work it held is retried.

panels.title: Goroutines
panels.description:
**How many concurrent tasks the program is running.**

**Normal:** grows during a scan and returns to a low, steady number after. A count that keeps growing between scans is a leak.

panels.title: Heap In-Use
panels.description:
**Memory used by the program's own data.**

**Normal:** rises during work and drops after garbage collection. Steadily rising floors across scans mean something is being kept.

panels.title: GC Pause — max & median
panels.description:
**How long the program stops to clean up memory.** Max = the worst pause, median = a typical one.

**Normal:** milliseconds. Pauses of hundreds of milliseconds mean memory pressure.

panels.title: Open vs Max FDs
panels.description:
**Open files and network connections against the process limit.**

**Normal:** far below the limit. Each PostgreSQL connection is one of these — and it is the closest thing to a connection count this connector has: a scan keeps up to 20 connections per database it reads, per pod, closing idle ones after ~2.5 minutes.

panels.title: OS Threads
panels.description:
**Operating-system threads the program uses.**

**Normal:** a small, steady number. Growing steadily means calls are blocking.

panels.title: Probe Duration by Depth
panels.description: Time spent discovering objects (databases, schemas, tables, columns) after the connection is open, by requested depth. Credential fetch and the connect itself are excluded.

panels.title: Peak Tests In Flight
panels.description: Most connection tests this connector was answering at once in the selected range.

### Oracle Connector — Overview
Generated from `dashboards/applications/V2/connectors/oracle/oracle-overview.json` · per-cluster board: [Oracle Connector — Overview](/d/apps-v2-oracle-overview)

**Totals add up every scan in the time range.** Two scans of a 13-owner database read 26 owners. To count what the database holds, narrow the range to one scan.

**Bars and stats say _how many_. The line charts beside them say _when_.** A scan shorter than ~30 seconds can be invisible on a line chart and still be fully counted in the bars.

**What this board cannot tell you:** anything per datasource or per owner (Oracle's metrics carry neither label — the DLQ messages do name the owner), and how many PDBs were scanned (with a credential to a single PDB, everything here is inside that one PDB).

Hover the ⓘ on any panel for what it counts, what is normal, and where to look next.

panels.title: Scan Duration ±15 s
panels.description:
**How long the scan took, end to end**: from the moment its owners were queued to the last table read. With several scans in the range it spans all of them, idle gaps included.

**Normal:** seconds to minutes. Precise to about ±15 s, because it is measured from samples taken every 10–30 s — a scan of a few seconds can read 0 s or 15 s. Owners run in parallel, so a small database really does finish in seconds (the local test database: about 5 s).

**Next:** 'Fan-out over time' in the Scanner row shows the same span as a shape.

targets.expr: max_over_time(timestamp(sum(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)) > 0)[$__range:15s]) - min_over_time(timestamp(sum(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_owners_published_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_owners_published_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_owners_published_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)) > 0)[$__range:15s])

panels.title: Objects Scanned
panels.description:
**Tables and views whose columns were read successfully.**

**Normal:** the tables + views of every scanned owner, once per scan in the range.

**Next:** 'Objects Failed' beside it; the funnel splits them by outcome.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Columns Found
panels.description:
**Columns read across all scanned tables and views.** Each one becomes a document.

**Normal:** roughly objects × average width (see 'Columns per Object' on the Pipeline board).

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_columns_found_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_columns_found_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_columns_found_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Documents Sent
panels.description:
**Documents handed on for indexing: one per column, plus one per table or view.** It counts documents sent, not distinct tables — the same table scanned twice is sent twice.

**Normal:** exactly Columns Found + Objects Scanned.

**Next:** 'Documents (window)' in the funnel, to see the two kinds apart.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_items_sent_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_items_sent_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_items_sent_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Objects Failed
panels.description:
**Tables or views whose columns could not be read.**

**Normal:** 0. Temporary failures are retried by rescanning the whole owner; permanent ones (permissions, broken definitions) are skipped and reported.

**Next:** the Scan Completeness row splits temporary from permanent.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_table_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_table_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_table_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Content Fetches
panels.description:
**Column samples requested from the content side**, any outcome. Content runs on its own pods, triggered separately from scans.

**Normal:** whatever the downstream classifier asked for; 0 when nothing requested samples.

**Next:** the Content row.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_content_requests_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_content_requests_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_content_requests_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Owners Queued
panels.description:
**Owners put on the queue to be scanned** — the start of the funnel.

**Normal:** the number of non-system schemas per scan.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_owners_published_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_owners_published_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_owners_published_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Owner Forks
panels.description:
**Attempts to scan an owner — not owners.** An owner that fails temporarily is retried, up to 5 times, and every try counts here.

**Normal:** equal to Owners Published. Well above it means owners are failing and being retried.

**Next:** 'NATS Redelivered' and 'Owners in DLQ'.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_schema_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_schema_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_schema_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Owners in DLQ
panels.description:
**Owners that failed all 5 attempts and were given up on.** Each one is a whole schema that was not indexed — while its scan still reports success.

**Normal:** 0. The board cannot name them; each message in the dead-letter queue does: `nats stream get DLQ_CONSUME_ORACLE <seq>` shows the owner and the last error.

**Next:** the Dead Letter Queue row at the bottom.

panels.title: Owners Done
panels.description:
**Owners published minus owners lost.** Nothing counts a successful owner directly, so this is a subtraction.

**Normal:** equal to Owners Published once the scan has finished. While it is still running it also includes owners not done yet.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_owners_published_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_owners_published_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_owners_published_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0)) - ((max_over_time(max(nats_stream_last_seq{stream_name="DLQ_CONSUME_ORACLE"})[$__range:30s]) - min_over_time(max(nats_stream_last_seq{stream_name="DLQ_CONSUME_ORACLE"})[$__range:30s])) or vector(0))

panels.title: Empty Owners
panels.description:
**Owners that have no tables or views** (or none the scan account is allowed to see).

**Normal:** some — service accounts often own nothing. A sudden jump on a database that used to have data usually means the scan account lost a permission.

**Next:** 'Scans Without DBA' in Scan Completeness.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_empty_scan_outcomes_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", scope="owner"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_empty_scan_outcomes_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", scope="owner"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_empty_scan_outcomes_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", scope="owner"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Objects Found
panels.description:
**Tables and views found in the owners: read + failed.**

**Normal:** equal to Objects Scanned when nothing failed. Retries list the same table again, so under retries it counts more than exist.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) + ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_table_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_table_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_table_errors_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Table Docs %
panels.description:
**Does every table get its own document?** Each scanned table or view should produce exactly one table document.

**Normal:** 100%. Lower means table documents stopped going out while column documents kept flowing — the scan still looks green, and this is the only place it shows.

**Next:** 'Documents (window)' below.

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_items_sent_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", kind="table"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_items_sent_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", kind="table"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_items_sent_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", kind="table"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) / (sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) > 0)

panels.title: Column Docs %
panels.description:
**Does every column get its own document?**

**Normal:** 100%. Lower means column documents failed to go out.

**Next:** 'Documents (window)' below.

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_items_sent_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", kind="column"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_items_sent_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", kind="column"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_items_sent_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", kind="column"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) / (sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_columns_found_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_columns_found_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_columns_found_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) > 0)

panels.title: Objects by Outcome (window)
panels.description:
**What happened to every table and view found.** Scanned = columns read. Failed — transient = a temporary problem (connection, timeout); the owner is retried. Failed — permanent = permissions or a broken definition; retrying will not help. Empty table = it disappeared or lost permissions between listing and reading (a subset of scanned).

**Normal:** all green. Orange needs a permission or schema fix; red needs a look at the database's health.

((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_empty_scan_outcomes_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", scope="pdb"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_empty_scan_outcomes_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", scope="pdb"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_empty_scan_outcomes_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", scope="pdb"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_empty_scan_outcomes_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", scope="owner"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_empty_scan_outcomes_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", scope="owner"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_empty_scan_outcomes_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", scope="owner"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_empty_scan_outcomes_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", scope="table"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_empty_scan_outcomes_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", scope="table"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_empty_scan_outcomes_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", scope="table"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: PDBs Skipped by reason (window)
panels.description:
**Why a PDB was left out.** not_listed = closed or dropped mid-scan. credential = the account cannot log in there. listing_denied = it can log in but cannot list. identity_mismatch = its service name leads to another database. no_pdb = an internal bug.

**Normal:** empty.

targets.expr: ((sum by (reason) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_pdbs_skipped_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_pdbs_skipped_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_pdbs_skipped_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) > 0) or vector(0))

panels.title: Errors Not Reported by reason
panels.description:
**Why error reports were lost.** buffer_full = errors came in faster than they could be sent. after_close / flush_timeout = they arrived after the owner had already finished (flush_timeout is the worst: they were abandoned). no_api = the reporter was never connected.

**Normal:** empty.

targets.expr: ((sum by (reason) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_error_reporter_dropped_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_error_reporter_dropped_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_error_reporter_dropped_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) > 0) or vector(0))

panels.title: Extended Metadata Degradations (window)
panels.description:
**Which optional detail was not collected, and why.** parameter_off = HEAT_MAP is off in the database, so last-used dates do not exist (a setting, not a fault). scope_all = the scan had no DBA access, so none of the details were collected. not_readable = missing grant. query_failed / probe_failed = the query errored. circuit_open = it failed for enough owners that the scan stopped trying.

**Normal:** empty, or only heat_map / parameter_off.

targets.expr: sum by (capability, reason) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_extended_metadata_degradations_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_extended_metadata_degradations_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_extended_metadata_degradations_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) > 0

panels.title: Extended Metadata Retries by source (rate, 5m)
panels.description:
**Optional-detail queries that failed once and worked on retry.** They never count as degraded, so this is the only trace.

**Normal:** empty. A rising line is the warning that the database is getting slow enough for the next retry to fail too.

panels.title: Pods Up
panels.description:
**Content pods answering right now.**

**Normal:** 0 when idle — content also scales to zero.

panels.title: Restarts (1h)
panels.description:
**Content container restarts in the last hour.**

**Normal:** 0.

panels.title: Fetches
panels.description:
**Column samples requested**, any outcome.

**Normal:** whatever was asked for.

**Next:** 'Content Fetches by Outcome' below.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_content_requests_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_content_requests_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_content_requests_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Content Fetch — mean / p95
panels.description:
**How long one sample takes**, end to end. Mean = the typical one; multiply by the number of columns to estimate a bigger job. p95 = the slowest 5%.

**Normal:** well under a second. Sampling cost grows with the size of the TABLE, so every column of a big table is slow.

**Next:** the Pipeline board for the streaming part on its own.

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_content_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_content_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_content_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) / clamp_min(sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_content_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_content_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_content_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])), 1)

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_content_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_content_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_content_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])))

panels.title: Errors
panels.description:
**Samples that did not succeed**, for any reason.

**Normal:** 0, but not every error is a problem — see the colours in the breakdown.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_content_requests_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", outcome!="success"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_content_requests_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", outcome!="success"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_content_requests_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", outcome!="success"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Fetch Backlog
panels.description:
**Bulk sample requests waiting** (the classifier's queue).

**Normal:** 0 between jobs.

panels.title: UI Backlog
panels.description:
**'See content' requests waiting** — a person in the UI is waiting on each of these.

**Normal:** 0 almost always. Anything else means someone is staring at a spinner.

panels.title: Content Fetches by Outcome (window)
panels.description:
**What happened to every sample request.** Green = fine. Yellow = expected (the column or table no longer exists, or the sample is over the size limit). Orange = configuration (bad request, credential, permission). Red = needs a look.

**Normal:** mostly green. Note: read_error also includes columns whose type cannot be sampled at all (LONG, LONG RAW, BFILE, XMLTYPE) — those are expected, not a database failure.

**Next:** 'Unsupported Types' in Sample Quality tells how many of the read_errors are that.

targets.expr: sum by (outcome) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_content_requests_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_content_requests_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_content_requests_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) > 0

panels.title: Content Fetches by Outcome (rate, 5m)
panels.description:
**When samples happened and how they ended**, same colours as the bars beside it.

**Normal:** bursts when a classification job runs.

panels.title: Content — In Flight & Connections
panels.description:
**How busy the content pods are.**

**Normal:** at most 4 samples at once per pod (CONTENT_FETCH_WORKERS) and 10 connections (ORACLE_POOL_WORKERS).

panels.title: NATS — Content Consumer Backlog
panels.description:
**Both content queues over time**: bulk (classifier) and interactive (a person waiting in the UI).

**Normal:** spikes that drain to 0. Each request is retried at most 3 times.

panels.title: KEDA — Content Replicas: current vs desired vs max
panels.description:
**Content pods running, wanted, and the ceiling** (10 by default, versus 3 for the scanner).

**Normal:** 0 when idle.

panels.title: KEDA — Content Trigger Signals
panels.description:
**What the content autoscaler looks at.** The interactive rule exists so a single 'See content' request wakes the pods even when nothing else is queued.

**Normal:** far below the thresholds in the legend.

panels.title: Samples Recovered
panels.description:
**Random samples that came back empty although the column has data**, rescued by reading the whole column instead.

**Normal:** common on small tables — 10% of a 3-row table is usually no rows. On big tables it means the sample percentage (ORACLE_CONTENT_SAMPLE_PERCENT) is too low for how sparse the data is.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_content_sample_verify_empty_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", outcome="recovered"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_content_sample_verify_empty_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", outcome="recovered"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_content_sample_verify_empty_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", outcome="recovered"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Empty Columns
panels.description:
**Columns with nothing to sample**: every value is NULL, or every value is an empty LOB.

**Normal:** some. Expected, not a failure.

**Next:** the breakdown below.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_content_sample_verify_empty_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", outcome=~"empty|unrendered"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_content_sample_verify_empty_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", outcome=~"empty|unrendered"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_content_sample_verify_empty_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", outcome=~"empty|unrendered"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Mean Sample Attempts
panels.description:
**How many tries a sample needs on average**, from 1 to 4 (4 = it had to read the whole column).

**Normal:** close to 1. Drifting up means samples keep coming back too small and are being redrawn.

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_content_sample_attempts_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_content_sample_attempts_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_content_sample_attempts_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) / clamp_min(sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_content_sample_attempts_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_content_sample_attempts_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_content_sample_attempts_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])), 1)

panels.title: Values Cut
panels.description:
**Sampled values longer than 4000 characters, cut to that length** (ORACLE_CONTENT_MAX_VALUE_CHARS). The classifier only saw the beginning of these.

**Normal:** 0 unless there are long text or CLOB columns. Sensitive data past character 4000 is not seen.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_content_values_truncated_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_content_values_truncated_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_content_values_truncated_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Unsupported
panels.description:
**Columns whose type cannot be sampled at all** (LONG, LONG RAW, BFILE, XMLTYPE, object types). They are reported as read_error.

**Normal:** expected on legacy schemas; not a fault.

**Next:** the breakdown by type below.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_content_unsupported_types_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_content_unsupported_types_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_content_unsupported_types_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Hit Size Cap
panels.description:
**Samples that stopped early because they reached the size limit** (ORACLE_CONTENT_MAX_SIZE_BYTES, 100 MB). The sample is still valid — it just has fewer rows.

**Normal:** 0.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_content_sample_budget_stopped_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_content_sample_budget_stopped_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_content_sample_budget_stopped_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Read Crashes
panels.description:
**Times the code reading rows from Oracle crashed and recovered.** The request shows up as read_error, but the cause was a bug in the connector, not the database.

**Normal:** 0. Anything else is a connector bug to report.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_content_producer_panics_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_content_producer_panics_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_content_producer_panics_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Empty Samples by kind (window)
panels.description:
**Why a sample came back with no rows.** empty = the column really is all NULL. unrendered = it has values, but every one is empty (e.g. EMPTY_CLOB()); an empty sample was uploaded. recovered = the random sample missed data that exists, and reading the whole column found it.

**Normal:** yellow is expected; orange is fine on small tables and a tuning hint on big ones.

targets.expr: ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_content_sample_verify_empty_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", outcome="empty"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_content_sample_verify_empty_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", outcome="empty"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_content_sample_verify_empty_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", outcome="empty"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_content_sample_verify_empty_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", outcome="unrendered"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_content_sample_verify_empty_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", outcome="unrendered"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_content_sample_verify_empty_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", outcome="unrendered"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_content_sample_verify_empty_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", outcome="recovered"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_content_sample_verify_empty_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", outcome="recovered"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_content_sample_verify_empty_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", outcome="recovered"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Unsupported Types by type (window)
panels.description:
**Which column types could not be sampled.**

**Normal:** LONG and LONG RAW on old schemas; anything else is worth a look.

targets.expr: sum by (data_type) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_content_unsupported_types_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_content_unsupported_types_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_content_unsupported_types_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) > 0

panels.title: Sample Size — rows and KiB per sample (mean, 5m)
panels.description:
**How big the successful samples were**, on average.

**Normal:** between 100 and 1000 rows (ORACLE_CONTENT_SAMPLE_MIN_ROWS / MAX_ROWS); fewer on small tables.

panels.title: DLQ Depth
panels.description:
**Scan work that was given up on and is sitting in the dead-letter queue now.** Each message is a scan request or a whole owner that failed 5 times — a whole schema not indexed while the scan reported success.

**Normal:** 0. To see which owners: each message names the owner and the last error — `nats stream get DLQ_CONSUME_ORACLE <seq>`.

**Next:** 'Owners in DLQ' in the funnel counts the ones added in the selected range.

panels.title: DLQ Depth over time
panels.description:
**When work started landing in the dead-letter queue.**

**Normal:** flat at 0. A step up marks the moment a scan started losing owners.

options.content:
### Oracle Connector — Pipeline
Generated from `dashboards/applications/V2/connectors/oracle/oracle-pipeline.json` · per-cluster board: [Oracle Connector — Pipeline](/d/apps-v2-oracle-pipeline)

**This is the drill-down.** The Overview says *what happened*; this board says *how much it cost* and *how it was distributed*. Nothing here is repeated from the Overview.

**Totals add up every scan in the time range** — narrow the range to one scan to describe one database.

**Heatmaps show one cell per owner or per query**, so a single slow one stands out instead of disappearing into an average.

Hover the ⓘ on any panel for what it counts, what is normal, and where to look next.

panels.title: Time per Object
panels.description:
**Average time to scan one table or view**, in milliseconds, end to end inside its owner: listing, reading its columns, sending its documents, plus its share of the owner's fixed cost.

**Normal:** a few hundred ms. Multiply by the number of tables to estimate a bigger database. It is the same total time as 'Time per Column' beside it, divided by tables instead of columns — so Time per Object ≈ Time per Column × Columns per Object.

**Next:** 'Time per Column' beside it.

targets.expr: 1000 * sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_schema_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_schema_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_schema_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) / clamp_min(sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])), 1)

panels.title: Time per Column
panels.description:
**The same total time divided by columns instead of tables**, in milliseconds. It is not how long one column takes to read — columns are read together, one query per table.

**Normal:** tens of ms. If it stays flat while Time per Object moves, the tables got wider, not slower.

targets.expr: 1000 * sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_schema_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_schema_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_schema_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) / clamp_min(sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_columns_found_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_columns_found_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_columns_found_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])), 1)

panels.title: Objects per Owner
panels.description:
**Average tables and views per owner**, counting only owners that have some.

**Normal:** any number — but databases are rarely uniform. One big owner hides inside an average.

**Next:** the 'Owner Duration — distribution' heatmap below shows each owner as a cell.

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) / clamp_min(sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_schema_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_schema_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_schema_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) - ((sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_empty_scan_outcomes_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", scope="owner"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_empty_scan_outcomes_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", scope="owner"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_empty_scan_outcomes_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", scope="owner"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s]))) or vector(0)), 1)

panels.title: Columns per Object
panels.description:
**Average width of a table**, in columns.

**Normal:** any number. A very wide table (hundreds of columns) moves this and the cost per table together.

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_columns_found_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_columns_found_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_columns_found_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])) / clamp_min(sum(sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_tables_scanned_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__range:15s])), 1)

panels.title: Owner Duration — distribution
panels.description:
**How long each owner took, over time.** **How to read it:** time runs left to right, duration bottom to top. Each box is 'this many owners took this long, at this moment' — the colour says how many (brighter = more), and hovering a box shows the exact number as Value. Colours do not identify individual owners.

**Normal:** one tight band when owners are similar. Boxes far above the band are the slow owners — the board cannot name them.

**Next:** 'Owners by Duration' beside it gives the same counts for the whole range, easier to read for a single scan.

targets.expr: sum by (le) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_schema_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_schema_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_schema_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod"}[15s]) * 1)[$__interval:15s]))

panels.title: Owners by Duration (window)
panels.description:

panels.description:
**How long each SQL query took, over time**, filtered by the Query type selector at the top. **How to read it:** time runs left to right, duration bottom to top. Each box is 'this many queries took this long, at this moment' — the colour says how many (brighter = more), and hovering a box shows the exact number as Value. Colours do not identify individual queries.

**Normal:** most boxes low. Column queries run once per table, so they dominate the count.

targets.expr: sum by (le) (sum_over_time(((last_over_time(oracle_scanner_query_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", query_type=~"$oracle_query_type"}[15s]) - last_over_time(oracle_scanner_query_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", query_type=~"$oracle_query_type"}[1d] offset 15s)) >= 0 or last_over_time(oracle_scanner_query_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", query_type=~"$oracle_query_type"}[15s]) * 1)[$__interval:15s]))

panels.description:
**How slow the slowest 5% of each kind of query was**, over time. list_tables runs once per owner, query_columns once per table, the rest once per owner for extended metadata.

**Normal:** only readable under sustained load. For a single scan use the mean beside it.

**Next:** the Overview's 'Query Time by Type' for where the time went in total.

panels.title: Query Mean by query_type (5m)
panels.description:
**Average time per query of each kind.** The average is the one that multiplies: average × number of calls = total time.

**Normal:** column queries well under a second.

targets.expr: sum by (query_type) (rate(oracle_scanner_query_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", query_type=~"$oracle_query_type"}[5m])) / sum by (query_type) (rate(oracle_scanner_query_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$oracle_pod", query_type=~"$oracle_query_type"}[5m]))
